title: Electric-field-driven magnetic switching and tightly bound interlayer excitons in bilayer CrSBr
authors: Xiubin Li, Yu Sun, Xuanji Wang, Chunyan Wang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Sheng Liu, Ting Yu, Liang Li, Tao Zhang, Jing Li
abstract: Electric field control of magnetic order in two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals magnets is a central goal for low-power spin-based technologies. In the ambient-stable antiferromagnet CrSBr, strong magnetic anisotropy and robust exciton-spin coupling provide a favorable platform, yet deterministic electric field control of its magnetic phases has not been achieved. Here we demonstrate electric-field-driven reversible switching between antiferromagnetic and ferromagnetic states in dual-gated bilayer CrSBr without intentional carrier doping. In parallel, photoluminescence measurements resolve a tightly bound interlayer exciton with an intrinsic dipole moment of only ~1 e angstrom. The electric field dependence of the magnetic phase transition reveals two coexisting mechanisms: a linear magnetoelectric effect in the antiferromagnetic state and an electric-field-modulated interlayer exchange coupling. Their interplay accounts for the asymmetric evolution of the critical magnetic field. Our results establish bilayer CrSBr as a promising 2D material for electrically controlled spin-optoelectronic functionalities.
summary: This work demonstrates electric field control over the magnetic switching between AFM and FM states in bilayer CrSBr. Using magneto-PL measurements, the authors characterize both the underlying excitonic physics and the magnetoelectric coupling mechanisms. The findings establish bilayer CrSBr as a highly promising platform for electrically controlled spin-optoelectronic functionalities.
main_problem: The central goal is achieving deterministic electric field control of magnetic order and understanding the interplay between excitonic states and magnetism in 2D van der Waals magnets for low-power spin-based technologies.
main_result: The study demonstrates reversible, electric-field-driven switching between antiferromagnetic (AFM) and ferromagnetic (FM) states in bilayer CrSBr. Furthermore, it resolves a tightly bound interlayer exciton whose behavior is coupled to the magnetic phase transition.
method: Magneto-Photoluminescence (PL) measurements are performed on dual-gated bilayer CrSBr samples while applying out-of-plane electric fields and sweeping magnetic fields.
model_or_system: The physical system is bilayer CrSBr encapsulated by hBN, studied in a dual-gated device structure. The analysis models the free energy difference between AFM and FM states as being governed by linear magnetoelectric effects and field-dependent interlayer exchange coupling.
key_observables: Magnetic phase transitions (AFM $\leftrightarrow$ FM), excitonic features ($X_a$, $X_b$, $X_i$), critical magnetic fields ($\mu_0 H_C$), and the dependence of these on applied electric field ($E$).
important_parameters: Temperature (3.7 K), Electric Field ($E \sim 0.03$ V/nm), Magnetic Field ($\mu_0 H \sim 0.3$ T).
main_assumptions: The asymmetry in switching behavior suggests involvement of localized states near the bottom layer under positive bias, and the magnetic transition is modeled by combining linear ME effects and $E$-tuned exchange coupling.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate abrupt spectral changes during field sweeps corresponding to phase transitions; PL spectra show electric-field-induced redistribution between excitonic species ($X_a$, $X_b$); and plots quantify the sign-dependent modulation of the critical magnetic field ($\mu_0 H_C$) by the applied electric field.
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents evidence for (1) reversible, electric-field-driven magnetic switching; (2) characterization of interlayer excitons coupled to magnetism; and finally, (3) a quantitative model explaining the observed asymmetry in the critical magnetic field dependence on $E$ by combining linear magnetoelectric terms and exchange coupling modulation.
why_interesting: The direct electrical control over magnetic order via excitonic signatures provides an experimental realization of multiferroic-like behavior in 2D materials, which is highly relevant for developing next-generation spintronic devices that couple charge/field to spin.
